title: Portfolio Heatmap with Elasticity Bands (PHEB) for capacity-aware roadmap allocation
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Problem: Our existing RICE-style scoring tables often fail to reflect hard capacity constraints (Dedicated pools) and non-linear latency penalties for user-visible features. Teams end up over-prioritizing high-opportunity features that are expensive at scale and create SLA risk.

Objective: Define and pilot a prioritization framework that surfaces capacity friction and latency elasticity alongside value signals, producing a portfolio heatmap that maps initiatives to 'elasticity bands' (low/medium/high token elasticity) and capacity regime (latency-sensitive vs throughput-oriented). The goal is to improve decision-making for Q2 roadmap allocations while preserving OKR alignment and enabling safer rollouts for Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Framework documented and reviewed by PM, Eng, and Solutions (Confluence doc + one-pager)
Pilot applied to 8 candidate initiatives for Q2 planning with clear bucketed recommendations (build/experiment/defer)
Top-3 initiatives selected using PHEB show >=10% lower expected token-cost risk vs baseline RICE selection in a Monte Carlo simulation
Stakeholder signoff (Head of Product, Head of Infra) on allocation recommendations and gating rules
approach: Define normalization of conventional RICE inputs (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) into a base 'Opportunity Score'
Introduce two new axes: Token Elasticity (sensitivity of cost to traffic scale) and Latency Regime Sensitivity (user-perceived latency risk), normalized 1..5
Compute a Capacity-Adjusted Opportunity = Opportunity Score / (1 + ElasticityWeight * Token Elasticity + LatencyWeight * LatencySensitivity)
Run Monte Carlo over traffic growth scenarios to generate a distribution of cost and p99 latency for each initiative when served under current Dedicated/Hosted mixes
Plot initiatives on a 2D heatmap: x=Capacity-Adjusted Opportunity, y=Expected 95th percentile token-cost uplift; overlay elasticity bands (Low/Med/High)
Convert heatmap buckets into policy recommendations: Immediate Build / Pilot+Measure / Defer or Re-architect
scoring_formula: OpportunityScore = normalize(R*I*C/E). CapacityAdjustedOpportunity = OpportunityScore / (1 + alpha*TokenElasticity + beta*LatencySensitivity). alpha,beta are knobs tuned per customer cohort (default alpha=0.5, beta=0.7). FinalPriority = CapacityAdjustedOpportunity * DeploymentMultiplier (hosts where dedicated=1.2, private=0.9)
sample_calculation: Example initiative A: R=80k users/month (normalized 0.8), I=4, C=0.7, E=3 => OpportunityScore ~ 0.8*4*0.7/3 = 0.746 => normalized => 0.62
Monte Carlo shows 90th percentile token-cost uplift of +44% under anticipated traffic -> maps to high-cost bucket => recommendation: Pilot with caching + quantization before full build

metrics: Mean and 95th percentile token-cost uplift vs baseline RICE pick
Number of initiatives reclassified to 'Pilot' because of capacity risk
Post-deployment p99 latency change for selected features (target: <5% regression),
Forecasted monthly dedicated GPU-hours consumed by selected roadmap items
risks: Telemetry completeness: we may not have accurate per-route token histograms which will bias Elasticity estimates
Stakeholder pushback: product teams may view added knobs as gating innovation; need playbook + exceptions
Modeling complexity: Monte Carlo inputs require credible distributions for traffic and model-size growth
Operational: recommended pilots may require infra work (autoscaling policy changes) introducing schedule slippage
